perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s subjective perspective, he has access to the following:

- He works with Teresa Ortega on a community service project in a professional/collaborative relationship.
- He noticed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He felt concerned, believed she needed help, and decided to offer assistance.
- He said: “Hey Teresa, I noticed you've been working really hard and seem a bit overwhelmed. Is there anything I can help you with?”
- He heard Teresa say she thought she could manage, but there was a lot to do.
- He told her it was important to take care of herself and offered to help so they could get through tasks faster together.
- He heard Teresa accept help with organizing medical supplies. He agreed and began helping.
- He believed Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathy and wanted to reassure her that accepting help did not undermine her abilities.
- He told Teresa he admired her desire to handle things herself, but accepting help didn’t mean she wasn’t capable.
- He heard Teresa say she wanted to show she could do it by herself. He responded that teamwork can make them more effective and that it was about getting the job done well.
- He heard Teresa agree and say she sometimes needed to remind herself of that. He said they were in it together and he was there to support her.
- He believed Teresa was still struggling despite his reassurance. He felt frustrated that his efforts weren’t yielding results and wanted another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- He told Teresa he could see things were still tough and did not want her to feel she wasn’t doing a great job.
- He heard Teresa say it had been a busy day and she felt behind.
- He suggested they work together on tasks instead of him just helping her. He heard Teresa agree. He said they should tackle it as a team.
- He believed working together would ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He felt hopeful and committed to the collaborative approach.
- He told Teresa he was hopeful the collaborative approach would make things easier. He heard her agree and say it already felt less overwhelming.
- He proposed handling inventory while Teresa managed patient records, with regular check-ins. He heard her agree. He said he was glad they were doing this together.
- He believed their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship. He felt satisfied with the outcome and intended to maintain the collaborative approach in future projects.
- He told Teresa their teamwork had paid off and suggested continuing collaboration in future projects.
- He heard Teresa agree, say it had been a great experience, and thank him for being a supportive colleague.

He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts, unspoken motives, or narrator-only details beyond what she stated and what he observed or believed.
